facts.fact: The EU Agency for Asylum report says the Somali ID is available as a physical card, a digital ID wallet called eAqoonsi, or a downloadable verifiable credential with a QR code, issued by the national ID authority NIRA.

SOM.note: No link between civil register and ID system is stated.
Birth certificates are mentioned only as an ID application document; no digital register stated.
No enrolment count or share given.
Number is issued at the end of an ID application, not at birth registration.
NIRA is said to manage the system but nothing on day-to-day operation, maintenance or code ownership.
No public register keyed on the ID number is stated.

facts.fact: The EU Agency for Asylum report says that after application and biometric capture NIRA issues applicants a unique 11-digit National Identification Number, and that card issuance was free as of 1 April 2026.

SOM.note: No other system checking against the ID is stated.
The World Bank team is quoted as unsure whether ID registration for the displaced segment is happening yet; no registration count or digital access stated.
Nothing on how local civil registration offices record events.
